subject: qilin
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: qilin, scaled hooved chimera with antlers and cloud mane.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning the design of a qilin creature combining deer and dragon features—scaled body, antlers, a swirling cloud-like mane, ox tail, hooves, dragon head with whiskers, and flame accents—while keeping the module compact at around 300 lines and working out proportions like shoulder height.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure: hip and spine joints, a neck chain leading to the head and jaw, a tail chain, and four legs built from multi-segment limb chains with carefully matched lengths and names so the reach from hip to ground works out correctly. I'm also sketching how the spine and neck will be built as catmull-rom chains with matching joint names, and starting to plan the head as a lofted shape with stations along its forward-facing direction.

Now I'm figuring out the finer details: a boxy dragon-like skull and jaw loft, decal eyes, bezier whiskers sweeping from the muzzle, antlers as swept branching spikes, and a cloud-styled mane made from textured cards and extruded puffs following frames along the neck sweep.

For the coloring I'm settling on a jade-teal scaled body with a cream-gold belly, white mane clouds tipped pink and gold, gold antlers and hooves, and glowing flame cards on the legs, plus a glowing pearl on the forehead using a glow kit import. I'm also planning helper loops for the legs and a four-joint tail chain ending in a flaming tuft.

Now I'm working out the head geometry, reusing the pegasus-style helper approach with a forward-down direction vector and loft stations defining a wide lion-like snout, along with eye decal placement on the skull.

Adding brow ridges, nostrils, fangs, and sweeping gold whisker curves with beard tufts under the jaw. For the antlers, I'm building catmull-rom paths per side with tapering sweep radii and spike tines branching off points along the path.

Now I'm working out ears as flattened spikes, then layering cloud-texture mane cards along the neck, shoulders, legs, and tail, plus bigger extruded cloud puffs and flame-glow cards at the fetlocks and hooves.

I'm placing mane card frames along the neck and body sweep curves with varied size, lean, and flow, then building the tail as a tapered chain with scale paint and clustering big cloud/flame cards near the tip.

For the body I'm applying scale texture with countershading between a jade top and belly tone, and painting the lower legs gold against the base coat. I'm shaping the spine sweep with a radius function for deeper chest proportions, then placing hoof cylinders at the leg tips just above the floor.

Now I'm working out the leg skeleton: front legs bend backward then forward across two inner joints for three segments, hind legs bend the opposite way, and I'm checking the reach from hip to hoof target lines up properly. For the hooves I'm splitting each into two small gold wedge boxes offset from center to get a cloven look.

I'm positioning flame-like fetlock cards angled back from each leg joint using oriented frames, adding a slight jaw rotation pose, and setting up a glowing forehead gem plus glowing flame cards while leaving the eyes unlit.

Now I'm planning a gold swirl emblem decal on the flank and sketching the body and neck sweeps, defining the spine control points and figuring out where the neck chain should attach to the spine joints.

Working out the tail chain with catmull points, the whisker curves as cubic beziers tapering to fine points, and the antler tine geometry, while keeping the eye as a golden-amber anime eye with a magenta iris.
